# Data shapes (a book's `data/*.json`)

Each book site publishes these as static files. They're the interface for the
app, the canon hub and any other tool (review F17). `data/manifest.json`
names the schema version of each file. A reader should check it and refuse
a version it doesn't know.

When a shape changes incompatibly, bump its number in
`biblecore/manifest.py` `SCHEMAS` and note the change here. Adding an optional
key isn't a bump.

Every file may carry a top-level `_note` string for humans. Readers ignore it.

## manifest.json (generated by the build)

```json
{"book": "Numbers", "slug": "numbers", "osis": "Num", "language": "hebrew",
 "versification": "kjv", "core": "0.3.0", "unit_count": 38, "units_built": 1,
 "files": {"units.json": {"schema": 1}, "...": {}}}
```

Optional: `"hub"` (the canon hub's URL) and `"overlay"` (book.json's secondary
grouping kind, e.g. `"discourse"`, drawn over the primary one by the app).

## units.json · schema 1 (the porter and `units-from-map` write it)

```json
{"book": "Numbers", "unit_count": 38,
 "groupings": [{"kind": "movement", "n": 1, "name": "at-sinai",
                "label": "At Sinai: ordering the camp", "span": "1:1–10:10",
                "units": [1, 2]}],
 "units": [{"n": 1, "slug": "unit-01", "passage": "Numbers 1:1–54",
            "title": "The First Accounting", "movement": 1, "built": true,
            "contract": "0.3.0",
            "roots": {"polls": {"color": "#55642f", "translit": "gulgolet",
                                "gloss": "…", "example": "…", "echo": "…"}}}]}
```

- Each unit row carries one integer per grouping kind in `book.json` `groupings`.
- `roots` holds **local** roots only. A tracked thread's colour lives in
  threads.json.
- `contract` appears on units ported at 0.3.0 or later, or migrated.
- Unbuilt rows have `built: false` and no `roots`.
- Passages and spans use displayed (English) numbering and an en dash.

## threads.json · schema 1 (hand-edited policy)

```json
{"version": 1, "threads": [{"id": "account", "root": "account",
  "translit": "paqad", "gloss": "…", "color": "#b1481f", "status": "open",
  "tagged": true, "note": "…",
  "opens": {"unit": 1, "ref": "1:3", "note": "…"},
  "payoffs": [{"unit": 14, "ref": "14:18", "note": "…"}]}]}
```

## roots.json · schema 1 (hand-edited policy)

```json
{"version": 1,
 "roots": {"account": {"ids": ["6485a"], "note": "…"}},
 "declined": {"<root>": {"why": "…", "date": "2026-09-23"}}}
```

`ids` are lemma ids: Strong's number plus OSHB's letter, with Hebrew and
Aramaic sharing one number space. In a Greek book they are transliterated
MorphGNT lemmas (`klēronomeō`), with a digit on a homograph (`tis2`); a bare
id matches every digit variant.

A phrase thread (no single lemma) gives `seq` instead of `ids`: an ordered
list of lemma ids, matched in order within `gap` words of each other
(default 4, never across a verse). `alt` adds further orders for the same
title:

```json
{"law-prophets": {"seq": ["nomos", "prophētēs"], "alt": [["prophētēs", "nomos"]],
                  "note": "…"}}
```

## occurrences.json · schema 1 (generated by `scan`)

```json
{"unit-01": {"account": {"count": 10, "verses": [3, 19],
   "hits": [{"v": 3, "pre": "…", "hit": "take account of", "post": "…"}]}}}
```

The keys are unit slugs, then root slugs. `v` is the verse number within the
unit's chapter.

## canon.json · schema 1 (generated by `canon`)

```json
{"intertext": [{"from": "Num 1:2", "to": "Exod 30:12", "kind": "echo",
                "unit": 1, "note": "root polls", "source": "echo"}],
 "typescenes": [{"id": "census", "ref": "1:1", "unit": 1, "note": "…",
                 "label": "…", "source": "meta"}]}
```

`source` is `echo` when a row was harvested from the fragments (re-harvested
every build), or `meta` when it came from a ported meta block.

## palette.json · schema 1 (hand-edited)

```json
{"well": ["#b1481f", "#2f5f6b"]}
```

This is the colour well in preference order, used by `colour` and the porter.

## components.json · schema 1 (generated by `assets`)

```json
{"components": [{"name": "echo", "role": "verse-aside", "selector": "aside.echo"}]}
```

`role` is `verse-aside` (collapsed into the verse note), `inline-block` (kept
in line, not hoisted) or `verse`. See `biblecore/components/__init__.py`.

## words/<ch>.json · schema 1 (generated by `emit`)

```json
{"c": 6, "verses": {"24": [{"w": "04Wfj", "t": "yebarek-ka", "l": "1288",
  "m": "verb, piel jussive, 3rd masc. sing. + pronoun suffix, 2nd masc. sing."}]}}
```

There's one file per chapter covering the whole book, not only built units. Words are
in text order, with Ketiv rows dropped. `w` is the OSHB word id (what `data-w`
points at), `t` the transliteration, `l` the lemma key (Strong's number plus
OSHB letter), `m` the morphology in plain words, and `"a": 1` marks an Aramaic
word. Verses use displayed (English) numbering. There's no native script.
In a Greek book `w` is MorphGNT's `bbccvv` plus the word's position in the
verse (`"01050501"`) and `l` the Greek lemma id (see roots.json).

## script/<ch>.json · schema 1 (generated by `emit`)

```json
{"c": 1, "verses": {"1": ["Βίβλος", "γενέσεως"]}}
```

Each word in the original script, parallel to `words/<ch>.json` (same verses,
same order, one string per word), for the interlinear's top line and nothing
else: the only place native script is written. Greek is MorphGNT's word
without punctuation; Hebrew is OSHB's with the morpheme slashes and the
cantillation dropped, the vowels kept. `verify-words` checks it lines up.

## lemmas.json · schema 1 (generated by `emit`)

```json
{"lemmas": {"1288": {"t": "barak", "g": "kneel; bless; curse", "n": 17,
                     "refs": ["6:23", "6:24"]}}}
```

`t` is the lexical form, transliterated. `g` is Strong's short definitions (up to three),
which are a word identifier and never a rendering. `n` is the count in the book, and `refs`
lists every verse, once each. In a Greek book the key is the lemma id, `t` the
id without its digit, and `g` the MorphGNT lexicon's gloss (its first sense;
empty when the lexicon has none).

## text.json · schema 1 (generated by `emit`)

```json
{"verses": [{"r": "1:1", "u": 1, "t": "Yahweh spoke to Moshe …"}]}
```

This is the study's own English for every built verse, with tags and endnote markers
stripped. Verses a component condenses (`data-verses`) have no entry.
